page: Amazon Web Services inf2.24xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server running on the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, delivering 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% tier. PassMark CPU encryption and memory scores also rank in the top 10% tier, demonstrating high cryptographic and memory subsystem efficiency. Single-core performance is moderately competitive, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the top 25% and middle 50% brackets, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for cached small-block reads in the top 25% tier, but drop to average levels in the middle 50% tier for larger, uncached read and write blocks.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high multi-core density, the inf2.24xlarge offers efficient resource density for parallelized workloads. It is optimized for database operations, software compilation, and text processing tasks. While it lacks local storage and hardware GPU accelerators, its 50 Gbps network baseline supports distributed architectures. It achieves strong results in Redis SET operations and prompt processing for smaller language models, making it a viable option for memory-cached applications and CPU-based inference pipelines.
